Ciechanow Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ciechanów, Poland

Demolished. This second, older Jewish cemetery in Ciechanów was established in 1771 on town-donated land; the Ordinary of Płock granted use rights in 1784, with first burials in 1797. Overcrowding concerns from 1822 led the community to seek adjacent plots; an 1846 tsarist edict mandating cemetery relocation outside towns coincided with this effort, though new land wasn't secured until 1873 after multiple failed transactions. Burials continued here until at least 1875, when Tzaddik Abraham Landau was buried beneath an ohel; in 1940, Jews secretly exhumed his remains and relocated them to the newer Pułtuska Street cemetery. Germans later completely destroyed this site, using forced Jewish labor to dismantle the fence and level the ground over 2 meters for new construction, repurposing tombstones for a sidewalk on 17 Stycznia Street. During 1939 leveling, Germans discovered a buried Torah and holy books, which they burned; four Jews who attempted to save the books were hanged at the castle courtyard.
